translation: Pallavi (Chorus):
Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries... Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries... Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries... Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries...
Mother, salutations to you... sweet love is yours... (Mother, salutations to you... sweet love is yours)
However simple a mud bowl you are... however simple a mud bowl you are... the cupped palms of your people are your earthen bowls too...
Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries... Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries...
Verse 1:

With the forests of Khammam-mettu she has wrapped a green sari... (wrapped a green sari) With Adilabad's crushed leaves she has put a mark on her forehead... (put a mark on her forehead) With the acacia in the middle of Nagaram she has lined her eyes with kohl... (lined her eyes with kohl) Grinding safflower petals, she has smeared herself with turmeric... (grinding safflower petals, smeared herself with turmeric) Telangana, the fully wedded woman... looks as if she has been widowed, mother...
Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries... Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries...
Verse 2:

See the turmeric-yellow, leaf-green hue of the black granite... (see the granite's hue) See the sweet, dear face like an old ruby steeped in nectar... (see the sweet dear face) See the smooth black sheen that mirrors the very gods... (see the smooth black sheen) Gold hangs from her sari's end, Singareni her heavy cluster of jewels... (gold on her sari's end, Singareni her heavy jewels) With plenty of mined gold in abundance... yes, with plenty of mined gold in abundance... she has learned to wear it plain, around her bare neck...
Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries... Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries...
Verse 3:

See the Kesulapuram fair where nine forms of Bhima are worshipped... (see the Kesulapuram fair) See Bhadrachalam, which bound together an angry Sita and a stubborn Rama... (which bound them together) See the form of Yamudaalaraajanna, worshipped in a single day chanting Siva Siva... (see the form of Yamudaalaraajanna) See the seven-branched fair where the Ganga split into separate streams... (see the seven-branched fair) See the Sammakka-Saarakka fair, where daughters are offered to great stone deities... (see the Sammakka-Saarakka fair) See the eyes of Gandimaisamma, of mother Poshamma, Kaashamma and Kaalemma... (see Gandimaisamma's eyes) See Komarelli Mallanna, hidden within the rock of Kondagattu... (see Komarelli Mallanna, hidden in Kondagattu's rock) She who has lit lamps for a crore gods... indeed, lit lamps for a crore gods... look at this mother who has no food of her own...
Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries... Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries...
Verse 4:

See the conch of the young cowherds that wakes everyone at dawn... (see the young cowherds' conch) Hear Mallur Kondayya's burrakatha, sung with tandana-tane on the tambura and burra... (Mallur Kondayya's burrakatha) Take the blessing of the fakir-sabs chanting 'in Allah's name'... (take the fakir-sabs' blessing) See the colours of the gangireddu bulls that bow again and again in salute... (see the gangireddu bulls' colours) Hear the oggu-katha of the Golla-Kuruma shepherds, with their plates and staffs going bheem-bheem... (the Golla-Kuruma's oggu-katha) Hear the tales of Yellamma told by the Bayindla with the jamidika going guruk-guruk... (the Bayindla's Yellamma tales) Hear the chirutala bhajana danced in steps under moonlit nights of kolatam... (the dancing chirutala bhajana) See the beats on the dappu drum, going jajjanakajan daddanakadan... (see the beats on the dappu) See the teenmaar's strike, see one dance-beat after another... (see the teenmaar's strike, see each different beat) This village of songs and dances... ah, this village of songs and dances is a mother who has no words of her own...
Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries... Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries...
Verse 5:

The great mother Mahabaleswaram gave birth to mother Krishna... (gave birth to mother Krishna) She embraced Maharashtra, the Tungabhadra, and the great stream Paleru... (the great stream Paleru) She wrapped around Ahalya, and kissed the Moosi river... (kissed the Moosi river) In Palamuru's lap, Krishna sang and played... (sang and played) On Nalgonda's heart she learned to walk, and she danced... (learned to walk, and danced) Rushing and roaring she came, and bathed in play at Jurala... (bathed in play at Jurala) Seeing Mallanna of Srisailam, she danced Siva's wild tandavam... (danced Siva's tandavam) In the heart of Nandikonda, the mother fell into a cool, quiet sleep... (fell into a cool, quiet sleep) But mother Krishna, to Telangana... our mother Krishna gave Telangana nothing but tears, no water at all...
Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries... Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries...
Verse 6:

In the nose of the western hills, that is the home where mother Godavari was born... (the home where mother Godavari was born) Making a vow at Basar, she set foot in Adilabad... (she set foot in Adilabad) Stretching out her hands, she lifted up the Kinnerasani and swept her along... (lifted her up and swept her along) She kept the Manjeera and the Kinnerasani hidden deep in her heart... (kept deep in her heart) She stretched out her hands, lifted them up, wiped their faces and kissed them... (wiped their faces and kissed them) At Pochampad she vowed to settle down and gave her word of assurance... (gave her word, gave assurance) But mother Ganga showed no mercy, she did not give even a potful of water... (showed no mercy, gave not even a potful of water) Mother Godavari, to Telangana... our mother Godavari left Telangana like a severed cord, motherless...
Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries... Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries...
Verse 7:

See the footsteps of the Gondu forefathers in the heart of mother forest... (see the Gondu forefathers' footsteps) See the feathers, see the spears of the mountain folk... (see the feathers, see the spears) See the dance of the Lambadi sisters, going yaadem-bodem-jimmeke-jimme... (see the Lambadi sisters' dance) See the Chenchu children, mother, faded flowers of the forest... (see the Chenchu children, faded forest flowers) See the Chenchu children, mother, faded flowers of the forest... (see the Chenchu children, faded forest flowers) The lush green mother forest... that lush green mother forest lies fully drowned in a pool of blood...
Mother Telangana, a song of hungry cries...
summaryEn: "Amma Telanganama" personifies Telangana as a suffering mother whose "song is a cry of hunger," structured as a pallavi with seven verses, each surveying a different aspect of the region. Verse 1 describes its districts and geography as a bride's adornments, yet says she looks widowed rather than happily married. Verse 2 dresses her in the region's stones and minerals, including the Singareni coalfields. Verse 3 catalogues major temple fairs - Bhadrachalam, the Sammakka-Saarakka jatara, Kondagattu, Gandimaisamma and others - closing on the image of a mother who lights lamps for a crore gods yet has no food herself. Verse 4 lists folk performance traditions such as burrakatha, oggu katha, gangireddu and teenmaar. Verses 5 and 6 personify the Krishna and Godavari rivers as mothers who nonetheless give Telangana "nothing but tears, no water at all." Verse 7 turns to the forests and tribal communities - Gonds, Lambadis, Chenchus - ending with the forest "drowned in a pool of blood." Categorized as a Movement song, it is a folk-catalogue of regional pride and grievance, particularly over water-sharing and neglect, central to the Telangana statehood movement.
summaryTe: "అమ్మ తెలంగాణమా" పాట తెలంగాణను ఆకలి కేకలతో నిండిన పాటగా బాధపడే ఒక తల్లిగా చిత్రిస్తుంది. పల్లవితో పాటు ఏడు చరణాలలో ప్రాంతంలోని వేర్వేరు అంశాలను వివరిస్తుంది. మొదటి చరణంలో జిల్లాల భౌగోళిక అందాన్ని పెళ్ళికూతురి అలంకరణతో పోలుస్తూ, అయినా ఆమె వైధవ్యం పొందినట్టు కనిపిస్తుందని చెబుతుంది. రెండో చరణంలో నాపరాయి, సింగరేణి బొగ్గు వంటి ఖనిజ సంపదను ఆమె ఆభరణాలుగా చూపిస్తుంది. మూడో చరణంలో భద్రాచలం, సమ్మక్క-సారక్క జాతర, కొండగట్టు వంటి ప్రసిద్ధ జాతరలను, గుడులను ప్రస్తావిస్తూ, కోటి దేవుళ్లకు దీపం పెట్టిన తల్లికే కూటికి లేదని ముగిస్తుంది. నాలుగో చరణంలో బుర్రకథ, ఒగ్గు కథ, గంగిరెద్దులు, తీన్మార్ వంటి జానపద కళా రూపాలను వర్ణిస్తుంది. ఐదు, ఆరు చరణాలలో కృష్ణ, గోదావరి నదులను తల్లులుగా చిత్రిస్తూ, అయినా తెలంగాణకు నీళ్లివ్వకుండా కన్నీళ్లు మాత్రమే మిగిల్చాయని చెబుతుంది. ఏడో చరణంలో గోండులు, లంబాడీలు, చెంచులు వంటి అటవీ, గిరిజన జాతుల జీవితాన్ని ప్రస్తావిస్తూ, అడవి తల్లి నెత్తుటి మడుగులో మునిగినట్టు ముగుస్తుంది. ఉద్యమ కేటగిరీకి చెందిన ఈ పాట, ముఖ్యంగా నీటి పంపిణీ, నిర్లక్ష్యంపై తెలంగాణ ఉద్యమ ఆవేదనను, ప్రాంతీయ గర్వాన్ని జానపద పట్టిక రూపంలో వ్యక్తపరుస్తుంది.
